parts.visual:
A small startup has 1,000 users. They want to reach 10 million users. They could spend 5 years buying Facebook ads. Or, they could convince Shopify (which already has millions of merchants) to integrate the startup's app directly into the Shopify dashboard. Overnight, the startup gains access to millions of users without spending a single dollar on ads.

The Symbiosis:
1. Riding the Giant: Startups have agility and cool technology. Massive corporations (Giants) have distribution and millions of users, but their tech is slow and boring. A strategic partnership allows the startup to trade their technology for the Giant's distribution.
2. The Danger: Giants are slow, bureaucratic, and often steal ideas. If a startup relies 100% on a single partnership, the Giant can change the rules one day and crush the startup instantly (Platform Risk).
parts.audio: A partnership is not putting two logos on a press release. A true strategic partnership is a deep, technical integration where both companies make significantly more money together than they would apart.

questions.question: What is 'Platform Risk'?
options: The existential threat of building your entire business on someone else's platform. If your startup only exists as an app inside Salesforce, Salesforce can simply build the feature themselves, ban your app, and destroy your company overnight.
questions.correct_answer: The existential threat of building your entire business on someone else's platform. If your startup only exists as an app inside Salesforce, Salesforce can simply build the feature themselves, ban your app, and destroy your company overnight.
questions.explanation: Never build your castle on another king's land.

questions.question: Listen to the BizDev (Business Development) executive. What is the fundamental rule of pitching a Giant?
questions.tts_text: Do not go to Microsoft and explain how much this partnership will help your startup grow. Microsoft does not care about your startup. You must explain exactly how your startup will make Microsoft's existing product stickier and more profitable.
options: You must ask for money nicely.

WIIFM (What's In It For Me). Giants only partner with startups to solve their own massive problems (like reducing their own churn rate). You must frame the partnership entirely around the Giant's strategic goals, not yours.
You must have a cool logo.
questions.correct_answer: WIIFM (What's In It For Me). Giants only partner with startups to solve their own massive problems (like reducing their own churn rate). You must frame the partnership entirely around the Giant's strategic goals, not yours.
questions.explanation: Elephants only dance if there is peanuts.

questions.question: What is a 'White-Label' partnership?
options: When a Giant uses your software but puts their own logo on it. The startup powers the technology in the background (getting paid handsomely), but the end-user thinks the Giant built it. Startups trade brand recognition for massive guaranteed revenue.
When a company only prints on white paper.
questions.correct_answer: When a Giant uses your software but puts their own logo on it. The startup powers the technology in the background (getting paid handsomely), but the end-user thinks the Giant built it. Startups trade brand recognition for massive guaranteed revenue.
questions.explanation: You provide the engine; they provide the paint job.

questions.question: Why do startups often die of 'Partnership Fatigue'?
options: Because negotiating with a massive corporation takes 12 to 18 months of legal meetings. A startup has 6 months of runway. The startup runs out of cash and dies while waiting for the Giant's legal team to approve the contract.
Because the Giant makes them run.
questions.correct_answer: Because negotiating with a massive corporation takes 12 to 18 months of legal meetings. A startup has 6 months of runway. The startup runs out of cash and dies while waiting for the Giant's legal team to approve the contract.
questions.explanation: Startups move in weeks. Corporations move in quarters.

questions.explanation: If you don't control the distribution, you don't control your destiny.
